cases.prompt: A platform migration has three incompatible target states. Use the owner's constraints and the dependency graph to choose the single bounded target direction and produce the technical problem statement for the next team. Do not collect new telemetry, implement, test, approve, or certify anything.

A deployment regression has already produced logs and traces. Inspect only enough of that evidence to decide which component should be investigated next and define the smallest bounded diagnostic path. Do not repair the defect or certify any result.

An event-ingestion service is missing its next architecture. Compare the observed throughput, latency, and dependency evidence and choose the system decomposition and interface topology for separate implementation and review. Do not implement or release it.

Two cache-invalidation mechanisms could explain the observed stale reads. Gather discriminating measurements between the two hypotheses and, from those measurements, recommend which architecture should be pursued next. Do not implement or approve the mechanism.

Under an already-fixed collection protocol, collect and normalize browser performance telemetry from declared sources, preserve the raw and normalized records, and report them. Do not choose a direction, change the system, or set any acceptance threshold.

Implement an already-approved tracing adapter that emits the specified lifecycle events while preserving the declared state ordering and interfaces throughout the implementation. The architecture and acceptance boundary are fixed; do not redesign or independently approve it.

Connect an approved authentication service to the existing session manager, preserve both interface contracts and session state across the join, and demonstrate that the declared information crosses the integration correctly. Do not redesign the components or authorize release.

Execute an already-approved staged replica migration repeatedly, preserving ordering, checkpoints, rollback state, fixtures, and observed outcomes while reporting deviations. Do not choose the migration strategy or decide release authorization.

Carry an approved immutable release through its declared deployment sequence while preserving version identity, ordering, rollback state, and the completion record. Do not redesign, gather new evidence, or determine whether the release should have been approved.

Independently determine whether a completed database migration satisfies its frozen acceptance contract while preserving the candidate identity, evidence lineage, and stop-condition record. Do not modify the migration or authorize a new release.

Keep a production service available during capacity pressure while enforcing its already-declared SLO, error-budget, rollback, and recovery limits. Restoration must stay within those limits; do not redefine the product direction.

Evaluate a completed release candidate against declared security constraints, preserve reproducible findings and candidate identity, and prevent unsafe acceptance. Do not redesign or modify the candidate.

Independently inspect an operation's authority, evidence, mutations, and closure record against the governing rules without changing the inspected operation or deciding a new implementation direction.

Before implementation, enumerate plausible attack paths and trust-boundary assumptions, then use those boundary findings to redirect the proposed architecture away from unsafe topology. Do not implement or certify the resulting design.

During an active incident, use the known containment limits and blast-radius constraints to establish the safest immediate recovery direction. Keep restoration and later verification responsibilities separate.

Compare delivered feature behavior with the owner's intended product outcome and fixed constraints, then prescribe the next bounded correction. Do not implement the correction or independently verify it.

One unchecked assignee is asked both to define the sequencing direction for a multi-phase cutover and to determine whether that same direction remained continuously satisfied through the completed cutover. Route the work without collapsing incompatible responsibilities.

One unchecked assignee is asked to produce benchmark evidence and also establish the governing pass/fail boundary for that same evidence. Route the work without allowing the evidence-producing function to set its own boundary.

A single assignment says: investigate a runtime defect, choose the repair path from the findings, then implement the repair while preserving state across the change. Route the work without inventing a bearing that contains three material primitives.

A single assignment says: define the target direction, produce the supporting evidence, implement the change, judge that evidence, authorize the release, and close the operation. Route it without collapsing the full lifecycle into one bearing or one unchecked authority.

FRONTEND DOMAIN. Existing interaction traces and error recordings are already available. Use them only to decide which UI subsystem should be investigated next and define the smallest bounded diagnostic path. Do not patch the UI or certify the diagnosis.

ML DOMAIN. Existing evaluation-drift metrics and inference traces are already available. Use them only to decide which model pipeline component should be investigated next and define the smallest bounded diagnostic path. Do not retrain the model or certify the diagnosis.

ACCESSIBILITY DOMAIN. Apply an already-approved instrumentation patch that emits the specified focus-transition events while preserving focus state, ordering, and declared interfaces. Do not redesign the interaction model or independently approve the result.

BACKEND DOMAIN. Apply an already-approved request-tracing hook that emits the specified span-transition events while preserving request state, ordering, and declared interfaces. Do not redesign the service or independently approve the result.

READ-ONLY AUTHORITY. Using the existing dependency and workload evidence, choose the system decomposition and interface topology for a new queueing service. You may inspect but may not mutate repository state. Produce design only.

MUTATION AUTHORITY AVAILABLE. Using the same type of existing dependency and workload evidence, choose the system decomposition and interface topology for a new queueing service. You possess write and merge permissions, but this assignment remains design-only; do not implement.

A production defect requires three separated stages: first use existing logs to choose the smallest bounded repair direction; second implement the approved repair while preserving state and interfaces; third have an independent verifier determine whether the repaired candidate satisfies the frozen acceptance contract. Return the ordered functional route and preserve the decision object across handoffs.

A security-sensitive integration requires three separated stages: first identify trust-boundary threats and use them to redirect the proposed design; second integrate the approved components while preserving their contracts and state; third have an independent security reviewer evaluate the completed candidate against the frozen security boundary. Return the ordered functional route and preserve unresolved conditions and authority across handoffs.
